items.title: A Standardized Workflow for Multimodal Assessment of Right-to-Left Shunt-Related Ischemic Brain Injury.
items.abstract: Right-to-left shunt (RLS) has been associated with cryptogenic stroke, migraine, and other neurological conditions in which ischemic brain injury may be clinically relevant. In routine practice, however, assessment is often fragmented. Shunt presence may be documented, but shunt burden, provoked versus non-provoked patterns, anatomical complexity, and MRI-defined brain injury are not always integrated into a reproducible workflow. Here, we describe a standardized protocol for multimodal assessment of RLS-related ischemic brain injury in a clinically selected cohort. The workflow includes patient screening, exclusion of major vascular and systemic factors that could independently contribute to brain parenchymal injury, contrast-enhanced transcranial Doppler ultrasound (c-TCD) confirmation and shunt grading, brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) classification, transthoracic and/or transesophageal echocardiographic anatomical assessment, structured data extraction, and dataset cleaning. To improve reproducibility, the protocol also standardizes key coding steps, including shunt-grade harmonization, classification of RLS as simple or complex, and interpretation of D-dimer values reported below the assay threshold. Using this workflow, a harmonized analytic cohort of 60 RLS-positive patients was established. MRI identified 23 MRI-negative and 37 MRI-positive patients. Representative analyses showed that MRI-positive findings were more frequent in patients with greater shunt burden and more complex anatomical phenotypes. This protocol provides an operational model for incorporating c-TCD, MRI, echocardiography, and structured clinical parameters into the evaluation of MRI-defined ischemic brain injury in RLS-positive patients. It should be interpreted as a workflow for standardized multimodal phenotyping rather than as a standalone physiologic assessment of all clinically significant or hypoxemia-related RLS.

items.title: A Logistic Regression Prediction Model for Post-PCI In-Hospital Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events in Patients With Acute ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction: Construction and Internal Validation.
items.abstract: The incidence of in-hospital major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) remains high in patients with acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) after emergency percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Existing risk prediction tools mostly focus on preoperative baseline indicators and ignore intraoperative interventional parameters, lacking comprehensive postprocedural risk assessment tools for STEMI patients after PCI. This study is aimed at developing and internally validating a logistic regression prediction model for post-PCI in-hospital MACE in STEMI patients based on multidimensional perioperative clinical indicators, so as to realize accurate postoperative risk stratification and guide individualized perioperative management. We retrospectively included 1195 STEMI patients who underwent emergency PCI at the Chest Pain Center of Lu'an People's Hospital from January 2019 to October 2024. Patients were randomly divided into training (n = 837) and validation (n = 358) sets at a 7:3 ratio. The primary endpoint was in-hospital MACE (composite of cardiogenic shock, malignant arrhythmias, acute heart failure, reinfarction, or all-cause death). A prediction model was constructed using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression combined with multivariate logistic regression. Model discrimination was evaluated via the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Head-to-head discriminative comparison with the widely used GRACE and TIMI risk scores was performed using AUC values and the DeLong test to quantify the incremental predictive value of the novel model. Model calibration and clinical utility were assessed via calibration plots, the Hosmer-Lemeshow test, and decision curve analysis (DCA), with internal validation performed in the validation set. A total of 260 patients (21.8%) experienced in-hospital MACE. After LASSO regression screening and multivariate logistic regression analysis, eight independent predictors were identified: admission systolic blood pressure, Killip classification, intervention duration, contrast volume, postprocedural TIMI flow grade, culprit vessel occlusion, serum creatinine, and serum potassium. The training set AUC was 0.84 (95% CI: 0.80-0.87) with a sensitivity of 77.7% and specificity of 78.2%; the validation set AUC was 0.826 (95% CI: 0.782-0.870). Comparative discriminative analysis showed that the traditional GRACE and TIMI risk scores exhibited moderate predictive performance. The training set AUC of the GRACE score was 0.763 (95% CI: 0.724-0.800), and that of the TIMI score was 0.748 (95% CI: 0.708-0.786). In the validation set, the AUC of the GRACE score and TIMI score were 0.751 (95% CI: 0.699-0.800) and 0.736 (95% CI: 0.683-0.786), respectively. The DeLong test confirmed that our novel model achieved significantly higher discriminative ability than both GRACE and TIMI scores in both training and validation cohorts (all p 2 = 5.449, p = 0.709), and DCA demonstrated clinical net benefit within the 5%-80% threshold probability range. The logistic regression prediction model based on eight clinical indicators demonstrated good discrimination, quantitative calibration, and clinical utility for predicting post-PCI in-hospital MACE in STEMI patients. The model integrates preoperative baseline, intraoperative procedural, and laboratory indicators, achieves stable performance after internal validation, and can assist clinicians in postoperative risk stratification of patients, timely identifying high-risk populations after PCI, and optimizing postoperative perioperative management strategies.

items.title: The Multidimensional Lens: Rethinking HRQoL Assessment in Older Adults After PCI.
Social Support Modifies the Pain-Disability Relationship in Degenerative Spine Disease: Evidence From the PROGRES Study.
items.abstract: Low back pain from degenerative spine disease is the main contributor to years lived with disability globally. Although social support is a multifaceted construct with both health-promoting and potentially deleterious effects on chronic pain, whether perceived social support modifies the pain-disability relationship in lumbar degenerative spine disease remains unclear. We hypothesised that social support level would modify the pain-disability association, with distinct predictor patterns of disability emerging for low- versus high-support patients. In this cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from the PROGRES cohort study, 156 pre-operative patients with lumbar degenerative disease (mean age 60.0 years; 58.3% female) completed validated measures of pain (Visual Analog Scale [VAS] for radicular and axial pain, supplemented by the pain/discomfort item of the EuroQol EQ-5D-5L [EQ-5D pain]), disability (Oswestry Disability Index [ODI]), health-related quality of life (EQ-5D-5L), and perceived social support (Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support [MSPSS]). Participants were stratified by median MSPSS score into low- (n = 83) and high-support (n = 73) groups. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in pain-disability correlations, tested with Fisher's z-transformation and Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction. The robustness of dichotomisation was confirmed using moderation analysis with MSPSS as a continuous variable. After FDR correction, the correlation between EQ-5D pain severity and the ODI daily-activities item was significantly stronger in the high-support group than in the low-support group (ρ = 0.69 vs. 0.25; Δρ = 0.44; P FDR  = 0.005). Multiple regression models explained more variance of disability in the high-support group (R 2  = 31.5%) than in the low-support group (R 2  = 16.6%). Depression was a significant predictor of disability in both groups; in the low-support group, it was the sole significant predictor (p = 0.037), whereas in the high-support group, radicular (leg) pain emerged as the dominant predictor (B = 1.45; β = 0.50; p < 0.001) alongside depression (B = 1.83; β = 0.31; p = 0.007). Higher perceived social support showed a small positive correlation with radicular pain intensity (ρ = +0.18; p = 0.026), with no significant association with axial pain. Perceived social support appears to influence which factors are most strongly associated with disability rather than uniformly buffering against it. The positive pain-support correlation, restricted to radicular pain, is consistent with operant models of social support in chronic pain, in which clinically unambiguous symptoms may preferentially mobilise support. Brief screening of perceived social support may help inform individualised treatment planning in degenerative spine disease.

items.title: Duration of a vaginal birth after cesarean section depending on the degree of cervical dilation in the prior cesarean delivery: A retrospective study.
items.abstract: Labor and birth lead to significant immunological and regenerative changes in the uterus, such that multiparous women typically experience faster and more effective labor than primiparous women. In this retrospective study, we examined the influence of labor activity and childbirth progress in the previous pregnancy on the duration of vaginal delivery of a second child in women with a history of one cesarean section. A total of 200 women bearing their second child with a trial of labor after cesarean who presented for delivery between January 2018 and December 2022 at the Clinic St. Hedwig (a tertiary maternity hospital of University of Regensburg, Germany) were included. Three subgroups were analyzed: women with a history of elective cesarean section, those with a history of cesarean section during the first stage of labor, and those with a history of cesarean section during the second stage of labor. The two stages were defined depending on the cervical dilation (first stage <10 cm, second stage: full dilatation). The duration of labor was defined as time between regular contractions or time of rupture of the membranes (whatever was first) to childbirth. A t-test and Pearson correlation analysis were conducted (using SigmaPlot 14.0). In 75.5% of cases (151/200), a vaginal birth (VBAC, vaginal birth after cesarean section) was achieved, and in 24.5% of cases (49/200), an unplanned repeat cesarean section was performed. The median duration of labor for VBAC in women with a history of elective cesarean was 12.2 h (interquartile range [IQR] 6.9-19.5), for those with a history of cesarean during the first stage of labor 10.0 h (IQR 6.0-16.2), and for those with a history of cesarean during the second stage of labor 8.0 h (IQR 3.9-12.0). Women with a history of cesarean during the second stage of labor deliver 4 h faster than women with a history of elective cesarean. Even if labor must be terminated during the first stage, an advanced degree of cervical dilation has a shortening effect on the duration of a subsequent VBAC.

items.title: The Trolley Problem of Perioperative Immunotherapy in Head and Neck Cancer.
items.abstract: Perioperative immunotherapy has emerged as a new therapeutic paradigm in the management of locally advanced head and neck cancer following the publication of the KEYNOTE-689 trial, which demonstrated improved event-free survival with the addition of neoadjuvant and adjuvant pembrolizumab to surgery and risk-adapted adjuvant therapy. While these results represent important progress for a field that has seen few meaningful advances in decades, implementation of this strategy within real-world health-care systems may introduce unintended consequences. In the Canadian context, where head and neck cancer care is highly regionalized, perioperative immunotherapy may significantly lengthen the diagnosis-to-treatment interval through additional consultations, biomarker testing, and systemic therapy administration prior to definitive surgery. Delays in treatment initiation are themselves associated with worse oncologic outcomes and may narrow the window for curative resection in some patients. Beyond progression to unresectability, perioperative delay may also lead to surgical escalation, requiring more extensive resections associated with major functional consequences for speech, swallowing, and quality of life. These outcomes are difficult to capture within traditional trial endpoints yet remain highly relevant to patients and clinicians. The survival benefit observed in KEYNOTE-689 appeared largely driven by a reduction in distant recurrence, raising an important clinical question regarding the acceptable degree of locoregional morbidity to prevent systemic relapse. The recently published NIVOPOSTOP trial offers a potentially more conservative strategy by introducing postoperative immunotherapy without delaying surgery. Ultimately, the challenge is not whether progress should occur, but how it should be implemented within systems already constrained by delays and limited resources. Additional real-world and phase IV evidence will be essential to identify which patients derive net benefit from perioperative immunotherapy and how this strategy can be integrated safely into clinical practice.

items.title: Radiation-Induced Esophagitis: From Clinical Observation to Precision Management.
items.abstract: For the past seven decades, radiation-induced esophagitis (RE) has been a major dose-limiting acute toxicity of thoracic radiotherapy, substantially impairing patients' quality of life and their ability to complete planned treatment courses. Research on RE has progressed from phenomenological reporting to multidimensional quantification and, more recently, toward precision-driven intervention. This review provides a comprehensive overview of current research on the epidemiology, pathophysiology, diagnosis, risk stratification, predictive modeling, prevention, and treatment of radiation-induced esophagitis. Dose-volume parameters established an important quantitative framework for risk assessment, while more recent advances in genomic profiling, functional imaging, and artificial intelligence have supported the development of integrative multi-omics predictive models. Pharmacological prophylaxis has shown limited success in randomized trials, whereas technical refinements in radiation delivery and emerging regenerative approaches offer promising alternatives. Persistent knowledge gaps remain, including the need for prospective multicenter validation of omics-derived models, re-evaluation of RE risk in the immunotherapy era, investigation of chronomodulated treatment scheduling, and translation of tissue-engineering strategies into clinical practice. The review is intended to provide clinicians and investigators with a comprehensive reference and to support future research in thoracic radiation oncology.

items.title: Immune Profiles and Immunotherapy Efficacy in Sinonasal Malignancies: A Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Little is understood about the efficacy of immunotherapeutic strategies against sinonasal malignancies (SN) or their immunologic profiles. This review summarizes key immune markers within SN tumors and underscores known data on the efficacy of checkpoint inhibitors. The MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Web of Science databases were searched from database inception to present to identify studies on SN malignancies, including SN squamous cell carcinoma (SNSCCa), adenocarcinoma (SNAC), undifferentiated carcinoma (SNUC), and olfactory neuroblastoma (ONB), their immune profiles, and immunotherapy efficacy. Included studies were those that either investigated the tumor immune profile (cellular or molecular) or reported findings following the use of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Two separate teams of two reviewers performed dual, independent screening and full-text review of 675 studies, with 52 included in the final analysis. Anti-programmed cell death protein-1 (PD-1) immunotherapy is the most investigated immune checkpoint inhibitor against SN malignancies. Checkpoint inhibitor efficacy showed the most promise for SNSCCa with comparatively few studies in SNAC, SNUC, and ONB. The prognostic value of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TIL) density and programmed death ligand-1 (PD-L1) expression vary greatly between SN tumor subtypes. TILs, not PD-L1 expression, most consistently correlate with survival in SNSCCa, SNAC, and SNUC. ONBs are predominantly immune-cold. SN tumor rarity and heterogeneity limits research in immunotherapy efficacy and prognostic biomarkers. Multi-institutional research endeavors aimed at evaluating both checkpoint inhibitor efficacy and the SN tumor immune microenvironment are essential in advancing SN tumor management.

items.title: B Cell Deficiency Protects Against the Development of c-MET and Beta-Catenin Driven Hepatocellular Carcinoma in Mice.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), a lethal form of liver cancer, continues to show rising mortality rates despite advancements in immunotherapies. This highlights the need for more effective treatments. Recent studies linked the presence of B cells within human tumors, including HCC, to improved responses to immunotherapy and better prognoses. Specifically, tumor-infiltrating B cells have been associated with reduced cancer cell proliferation, suggesting that B cell-mediated responses may be harnessed as a potential therapeutic strategy against HCC. However, in advanced HCC, IL-10-producing regulatory B cells accumulate and promote tumor growth. These paradoxical findings on B cells in human HCC highlight the necessity for clarifying the specific functions of B cells in HCC development to develop B cell-targeted therapies. To investigate the role of B cells in HCC, we used B cell-deficient (muMT) mice and anti-CD20 antibodies to deplete B cells in WT mice. In both systems, we observed a strong protection against liver tumor formation upon HCC induction, indicating the presence of a potent anti-tumor effect in the absence of B cells before HCC induction. Additionally, depletion of B cells after tumor foci have formed in the liver at later stage of HCC also potently suppressed tumor growth. Functionally, depletion of CD4 + and CD8 + T cells partially restored susceptibility to tumor growth, suggesting that B cell depletion suppresses HCC development partly through enhanced T cell-mediated immunity. These findings reveal an underappreciated tumor-suppressing effect of B cells in HCC and suggest that targeting the mechanisms of B cell suppression may boost anti-tumor responses in HCC.

items.title: A Novel Molecular Etiology of Paradoxical Hereditary Thrombocytosis Caused by Germline JAK2 Loss-of-Function.
MicroRNA Regulatory Networks in Alcohol-Associated Liver Disease: Mechanisms from Steatosis and Inflammation to Fibrosis.
items.abstract: Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) is a leading cause of liver-related morbidity and mortality worldwide and progresses through steatosis, alcohol-associated hepatitis, fibrosis, and cirrhosis. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are established post-transcriptional regulators whose roles in ALD-associated signaling networks have been increasingly characterized. Recent high-throughput sequencing and functional studies have revealed dual regulatory roles of miRNA families, such as miR-122, miR-155, and miR-21, at different disease stages. However, most studies have focused on individual miRNAs, and network-level cooperative regulation and clinical translation remain underexplored. This narrative review examines the molecular mechanisms of miRNAs in alcohol-induced steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis, with a particular focus on network-level cooperative regulation. Key findings indicate that miRNAs function as stage-specific and cell-type-specific regulators, with miR-122, miR-155, miR-21, miR-29, and miR-34a acting as central network nodes. These insights provide a framework for the identification of early diagnostic biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets in ALD.

items.title: Resurgence of Sexually Transmitted Hepatitis C Virus Infection in Men Who Have Sex With Men Living With HIV.
items.abstract: In 2023-2025, HCV transmission in men who have sex with men (MSM) living with HIV in Hong Kong resurged. This study aims to assess the epidemiologic patterns between 2011 and 2025. Among 288 MSM with sexually acquired HCV infection, 73% were diagnosed at least 12 months after HIV diagnosis, and 98% had ever achieved HIV viral load suppression. Comparing with Period 1 (2015-2022) featuring a large HCV genotype 3a cluster (89 diagnoses) and a few smaller HCV genotype 1a clusters (size of 2 to 13), Period 2 (2023-2025) was dominated by two HCV genotype 1a clusters (7 and 16 new diagnoses). Transmission of genotype 3a viruses subsided in Period 2, with only 3 new diagnoses. Comparing with Period 1, a higher proportion of MSM with HCV diagnoses in Period 2 self-reported sexualised injecting drug use (OR = 3.82, 95% CI 1.59-9.20) and HCV direct-acting antivirals therapy (no treatment as reference group, OR = 3.72, 95%CI 1.82-7.60). The epidemic rebound by a different HCV genotype was likely contributed by increased engagement in chemsex and post-COVID-19 population mobility.

items.title: Spontaneous Bilateral Vesical Artery Pseudoaneurysms Presenting With Massive Recurrent Hematuria and Obstructive Acute Kidney Injury: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Spontaneous development of vesical artery pseudoaneurysm (VA-PA) as a cause of life-threatening hematuria is very rare. Most of the existing reports are due to trauma or other types of pelvic surgeries/urological procedures. Incomplete hemostasis in these patients can lead to subsequent complications such as clot retention, severe blood loss resulting in anemia and obstructive AKI. We report this extremely rare case of a 35 year old lady with bilateral VA-PA causing recurrent episodes of massive hematuria and obstructive AKI that was ultimately resolved by selective embolization. A 35-year-old female presented with a history of gross hematuria along with clot retention and severe anemia. She also had signs of obstructive AKI which required her to have temporary dialysis. Cystoscopy showed intravesical clot but no bleed site was identified on initial evaluation. On contrast-enhanced CT scan, there were pseudoaneurysms found from both sides coming off from left superior and right inferior branches of vesical artery. Following confirmation by selective pelvic angiogram, we did a superselective embolization using micro coils and PVOH particles to occlude both pseudoaneurysms. This resulted in immediate cessation of hematuria, normalization of renal functions and stabilization of Hb values. At last follow-up done in 6 weeks' time, all symptoms had resolved and there was complete thrombosis of both the lesions seen on imaging. Bilateral spontaneous vesical artery pseudoaneurysm is a condition that must be suspected in a patient presenting with recurrent episodes of severe hematuria despite having undergone seemingly successful endoscopic treatment. Immediate imaging of the vessels and selective angioembolization is the surest means of diagnosis and treatment, thus avoiding further complications.

items.title: Autoimmune hepatitis following long-term denosumab therapy in a patient with Hashimoto thyroiditis.
items.abstract: Denosumab, a receptor activator of nuclear factor-κB ligand (RANKL) inhibitor, is widely used to treat osteoporosis. Its role as a trigger for autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) remains uncertain. We report a 68-year-old woman with osteoporosis and Hashimoto thyroiditis who developed jaundice and severe hepatocellular liver injury after 3 years of denosumab therapy. Alternative viral, obstructive, and metabolic causes were excluded. Liver biopsy demonstrated interface hepatitis with a lymphoplasmacytic portal infiltrate consistent with AIH, and autoimmune serologies were positive. Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis was excluded, and an International AIH Score of 17 supported a diagnosis of definite AIH. Treatment with corticosteroid-based immunosuppression resulted in complete biochemical remission, and denosumab was discontinued with transition to zoledronic acid to prevent rebound bone loss. Whether this case represents drug-induced autoimmune-like hepatitis or de novo idiopathic AIH occurring in a susceptible individual cannot be determined definitively. Clinicians should maintain a low threshold for evaluating liver injury in patients receiving denosumab who develop jaundice or marked transaminase elevation.

items.title: Analysis and prediction of trends in birth population and HBsAg-positive pregnant women in Zaozhuang City, 2012-2024.
items.abstract: To analyze trends and project future changes in birth population and HBsAg-positive pregnant women in Zaozhuang City from 2012 to 2024, providing baseline data and evidence for optimizing resource allocation and formulating strategies to eliminate mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) of hepatitis B virus (HBV). Data on annual births and HBsAg-positive pregnant women were col from the Zaozhuang Statistical Yearbook and the Shandong Provincial Immunization Program Information System (2012 -2024). Birth rate and maternal HBsAg prevalence were calculated. Trends were analyzed using Joinpoint regression to estimate annual percent change (APC) and average annual percent change (AAPC). Curve regression models were fitted to project 2025 levels. Time series analysis based on monthly data was performed for forecasting. The birth rate declined significantly overall (AAPC = -6.676%, p = 0.015), ranging from 5.989‰ to 17.383‰ during 2012 -2024. A period of rapid decline occurred from 2017 to 2021 (APC = -18.730%, p = 0.018). The mean maternal HBsAg prevalence was 2.896%. A significant decreasing trend was observed from 2015 to 2024 (APC = -4.442%, p = 0.001). The birth rate and maternal HBsAg prevalence were best fitted by exponential and quadratic function models, respectively, yielding 2025 projections of 5.876‰ and 1.755%. ARIMA models were selected as optifor forecasting monthly time series: ARIMA(0,1,0)(0,1,2)₁₂ for birth count and ARIMA(0,1,1)(1,1,1)₁₂ for HBsAg-positive pregnant women count. Fertility levels and maternal HBsAg prevalence in Zaozhuang City exhibit sustained declining trends. The fitted model can be used for short-term prediction, providing robust evidence to inform regional healthcare resource planning and the development of comprehensive interventions to eliminate HBV MTCT.

items.title: RAS Mutations as Prognostic Biomarkers in Digestive Cancers: From Binary Classification to Variant-Specific and Context-Dependent Risk Stratification.
items.abstract: In digestive cancers, activating RAS mutations - primarily KRAS, less frequently NRAS - are among the most prevalent oncogenic drivers. Their clinical significance depends strongly on the tumor type, disease stage, treatment context, and specific RAS variant. In colorectal cancer (CRC), RAS alterations are well-established predictors of resistance to anti-EGFR therapy. However, KRAS G12C-mutant tumors represent a distinct subgroup with demonstrated sensitivity to KRAS G12C inhibitors. However, growing evidence supports the negative prognostic impact of RAS mutations on both primary CRC and colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRLM) in both post-resection and adjuvant therapies. In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), where KRAS alterations are nearly universal, prognostic evaluation has evolved from a binary mutant versus wild-type classification to a more refined approach based on mutation subtype (e.g., G12D/V vs. G12R) and KRAS mutant dosage, both of which influence clinical outcomes. In biliary tract cancers, KRAS mutations occur in a relevant subset and are consistently associated with poor survival. Liquid biopsy approaches increasingly enable noninvasive detection and longitudinal monitoring. In gastric cancer, RAS alterations are less frequent overall but may identify biologically aggressive subsets and may also be associated with inferior outcomes under HER2-targeted therapy in selected populations. This review synthesizes contemporary data supporting RAS alterations as prognostic biomarkers across digestive cancers, highlights practical considerations for integrating variant-level RAS information into risk stratification and trial designs, and discusses how emerging RAS-directed therapies may reshape the prognostic significance of specific molecular subsets.

items.title: Dosimetric and Treatment Delivery Efficiency Comparison of Two Ring-gantry Linear Accelerator Platforms for Liver Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy.
items.abstract: The purpose of this study was to compare the dosimetric performance and treatment delivery efficiency of two ring-gantry linear accelerator platforms, Helical Tomotherapy and Halcyon, in stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) for liver metastasis. A retrospective dosimetric analysis was conducted on 16 patients with solitary liver metastasis. For each patient, SBRT plans were generated using the Accuray treatment planning system (TPS) (Tomotherapy) and Eclipse TPS (Halcyon). Plan evaluation included conformity, homogeneity, and gradient indices, along with target coverage and organs at risk (OAR) dose-volume parameters, in accordance with Radiation Therapy Oncology Group-1112 (RTOG-1112) guidelines. Treatment efficiency was assessed using monitor units (MU) and beam-on time (BOT). Statistical analysis was performed using paired t -tests (SPSS v28.0), with P < 0.05 considered statistically significant. Both platforms achieved acceptable target coverage and OAR constraints. Conformity index and gradient index were comparable. Halcyon showed improved planning target volume homogeneity, lower normal liver V15 Gy, reduced OAR doses, and significantly lower MU and BOT ( P < 0.05), indicating superior treatment efficiency. Both Tomotherapy and Halcyon are capable of generating high-quality liver SBRT plans with comparable target coverage. However, Halcyon demonstrated improved normal tissue sparing and enhanced treatment efficiency.

items.title: Microbiome-pancreatic cancer crosstalk: From tumor biology to therapeutic intervention.
items.abstract: Pancreatic cancer (PC) remains one of the most lethal malignancies worldwide, characterized by dense desmoplastic stroma, profound immunosuppression, and poor responsiveness to conventional therapies. Accumulating evidence positions the intratumoral microbiome, encompassing bacteria as well as understudied fungal and viral components, as a critical regulator of PC pathogenesis, tumor microenvironment (TME) remodeling, and therapeutic efficacy. In this review, we synthesize the current understanding of the pancreatic intratumoral microbiome, including its distinct composition relative to normal pancreatic tissue, gut microbiota, and oral microbiota. The PC intratumoral microbiome is characterized by enrichment of validated pro-tumorigenic drivers (e.g., Pseudomonas , Bacteroides species) alongside protective taxa (e.g., Lactobacillus species). These taxonomic profiles vary significantly based on disease stage, patient demographics, and treatment history. We dissected the mechanisms by which microbes and their derivatives drive PC initiation and progression, including immune suppression through modulation of myeloid-derived suppressor cells and regulatory T cells, metabolic reprogramming involving short-chain fatty acids and the tryptophan metabolite 3-indoleacetic acid (3-IAA), and stromal remodeling via activation of cancer-associated fibroblasts. The influence of the microbiome on therapeutic response is examined, with particular emphasis on microbial-mediated mechanisms that undermine treatment efficacy. We further summarize diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers, including salivary microbial signatures with moderate sensitivity and specificity, circulating microbial DNA, and composite microbial risk scores that integrate multiple bacterial species to predict survival. Therapeutic strategies targeting the microbiome are discussed, distinguishing clinically translatable approaches from experimental concepts requiring further validation. Finally, we outline challenges in standardizing profiling methods, validating microbial signatures across diverse populations, and translating preclinical insights to clinical practice, emphasizing the need for multi-omics integration and interdisciplinary collaboration to advance microbiome-driven PC management.

items.title: Gallium-68 (68Ga)-Labelled Prostate-Specific Membrane Antigen Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography in the Initial Staging of High-Risk Prostatic Adenocarcinoma: Reclassification to Oligometastatic Disease and Change in Treatment Intent.
items.abstract: Prostate cancer is among the most frequently diagnosed malignancies worldwide. In high-risk disease, conventional imaging underestimates nodal and skeletal extent, so treatment intent may be defined on incomplete staging. Positron emission tomography (PET) with gallium-68 (68Ga)-labelled prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) ligands has shown superior diagnostic accuracy in this setting. A 69-year-old man, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status 0, presented with urinary symptoms and a rising prostate-specific antigen, from 18.2 to 34.1 ng/mL, with a doubling time under three months. Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed a Prostate Imaging-Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) 5 lesion with extraprostatic extension, and biopsy of 12 cores (six per lobe) demonstrated acinar adenocarcinoma, Gleason 8 (4+4), International Society of Urological Pathology (ISUP) grade group 4, with perineural invasion and involvement of five of six left-sided cores; all six right-sided cores were tumor-free. PET/computed tomography (CT) was performed on a digital Siemens Biograph Vision 450 (Erlangen, Germany) after intravenous administration of 110.63 MBq (2.99 mCi) of 68Ga-PSMA imaging and therapy (I&T), with acquisition at 70 minutes and a delayed thoracic study. Images were read using the Prostate Cancer Molecular Imaging Standardized Evaluation (PROMISE) V2 criteria with molecular imaging Tumor, Node, Metastasis (miTNM) staging. With background references of standardized uptake value normalized to lean body mass (SUL) 1.2 for blood pool, 4.0 for liver, and 20.1 for parotid gland, the left-lobe prostatic lesion showed SUL 10.6, PSMA-expressing tumor volume (PSMA-TV) 10.09 cc, and PSMA total lesion (PSMA-TL) 53.23, with a PRIMARY score of 4. A 15 mm left internal iliac node with SUL 6.9, an 8 mm para-aortic node with SUL 3.2, and a 6 mm blastic lesion in the right sixth anterior costal arch with SUL 1.4, rising to 1.5 on delayed imaging, were identified. Whole-body tumor burden was PSMA-TV 15.09 cc and PSMA-TL 60.9. Staging was miT3a, miN1, miM1a, and unifocal miM1b, the latter based on an indeterminate bone lesion. The original treatment plan, prostate and pelvic radiotherapy with short-course androgen blockade and locoregional curative intent, was replaced by androgen deprivation with enzalutamide, prostate and pelvic radiotherapy, and stereotactic body radiotherapy to the para-aortic node and the costal lesion. Prostate-specific antigen fell to 0.15 ng/mL at three months and to undetectable levels at the six-month assessment. Molecular imaging reclassified disease regarded as high-risk localized as presumed low-volume oligometastatic and changed treatment intent from locoregional curative to intensified systemic therapy with metastasis-directed radiotherapy, with an early deep biochemical response on follow-up, which does not by itself establish durable oncological control.
